s: How the dock works and how to stay safe in the river. Your door code is at the end.
Free lot across from the marina at NE Bridgeton and NE 2nd. Follow the signs down the ramp to the dock.
check: Davey is sending phone video of the walk from the lot and down this ramp, for an accurate walk-through.

s: The sauna boat sits beside the lounge on the main dock. In winter the current usually runs this way. In summer wind and tide can turn it either way.
Enter at the landing. The Locker Lounge is beside it, the Downpour sits by the boat, and the social sauna has a ladder at each end. Red dotted lines mark the swim line.
Lounge by the fire, lunch tables, then the downriver dock and its ladder. The private saunas are past that.
Change in the bathroom, the shower, the room to the right of the shower, or under a towel in the covered lounge. Lockers by the bench, coats on the hooks, shoes stay here.
Snacks are fine out here and on the roof. Only water goes in the sauna. No alcohol on site.
No shoes in the sauna. Sit on a towel wherever skin touches wood, a towel under your feet on the benches too. Your door code opens the keypad.

h: Steam: one scoop at a time
s: Ask the room first, then pour. Fresh water only. Don't touch the stove, the rocks, or the controls.
check: Stove is natural gas. Never say wood-fired.

s: Pull the cord for a cold rinse between rounds. It sits on the dock beside the boat, where the boat's dock meets the main walkway.
check: Placed from the site plan. The photo shows the old spot, so send a photo of the Downpour where it stands now.

s: Dark, windy, too cold, not a strong swimmer? Skip the river. The sauna is the whole visit.
No staff and no lifeguard. Once you're here, you look after each other.
check: Send a clear photo of the no-lifeguard sign if you want it on this slide.

s: A life jacket or swim buoy on everyone who goes in, however well you swim. PFDs hang on the lounge hooks and next to the ladders.
Three ways out: the stair end of the boat, the far corner of the boat, and the dock downstream. Find them before you get in.
check: All ladders are in place and working. New ladders are on order.

s: Cold water makes you gasp. Get in slowly, hold the ladder and breathe slow until it passes.
check: New slide: moved here because the old gasp photo is the downriver dock.

h: Can't swim back? Ride to this dock
s: Let the current carry you to the downriver dock and climb its ladder. Never jump from this dock: the current sweeps you under it.
Never fight the current. Ride it to the nearest ladder. In winter it usually runs this way; in summer it can turn with wind and tide.
Push off hard, away from the boat, so the current can't pull you under the hull.
check: Capitol safety plan v3 says ladders only. The video allows feet-first jumps, so the insurer wording needs to match.

h: Off the roof? Take the stairs
s: Use the stairs, not the rail. Look below before you jump, and know which ladder you'll swim to.
One in the water, one on the boat within reach of a throw ring or rescue pole. Never go in after a panicking swimmer.
Throw the ring or reach with the rescue pole, then pull them to a ladder. A ring and a pole hang at each end of the boat. Never go in after someone.
check: Photo predates the pole. A new photo with the pole hung would be better.

s: Shorter when the water is cold. Get out before you go numb.
No alcohol. Walk, don't run. Dizzy? Sit down and stay out of the water. After dark, skip the river and use the Downpour and the shower.
The door code shows up once everyone in your party has signed, each with their own email and phone. Short a person? Someone can sign a second time to release it.
